description: Kind: captions Language: en DO UNTO OTTERS A book about Manners by Laurie  Keller Creatively read and adapted by Lorenzo Story time is fun! This is my way  of encouraging kids like me to read,   learn and have fun! Come join me for  a story time with lorenzo [Music]   Do on to others whoops otters This  book is based on the golden rule [Music] [Music]   Hello Mr Rabbit. We're your new neighbors, the  OTTERS! Otters, my new neighbors are otters. i don't know anything about otters.  What if we don't get along? [Music] boom pesky otters lousy rabbit  Mr rabbit i know an old saying: Do onto otters as you would have  others do onto you. What does that mean? It simply means treat otters the same  way you'd like otters to treat you. Treat otters the same way I'd like otters to treat  me. hmm How would i like otters to treat me?   How would I like otters to treat me? Well. . . I'd like otters to be FRIENDLY. A cheerful hello. Howdy neighbor   A nice smile and good eye contact blah  blah blah are all part of being friendly.  Friendliness is very important to me - especially after my last neighbor, Mrs. Grrrrrr.  Voted 'Meanest Neighbor' for six years a row. I'd like otters to be POLITE. They should know  when to say please. Please look. Yoohoo, Mr. Rabbit,   Would you please return my ball there?  PRETTY PLEASE with CARROTS on top? Would you like me to stop stinging you? Yes PLEASE. i can say PLEASE in five languages Por Favor (Spanish) "S'il vous plait" (French) "Bitte" (German) "Kudasai" (Japanese) "Easeplay" (Pig Latin) Impressive! impressive! Say the magic word and I'll turn  these clams into a MILLION DOLLARS!. 'Magic   word rhymes with this.' CHEESE, PLEASE. They should  know what to say THANKYOU. Thanks for looking. Dear Mr. Rabbit, Thank you very much for  returning my ball. You must have returned a   lot of balls before because you made it look  so easy. Balls sure are bouncy (and roll-y) but   I'll try to keep it under control next time.  Sincerely, Would you like me to sting you now? "No thank you." "Then please take my BEE-zness (business) card and tell me when you're ready. I can say THANKYOU in five languages "Gracias" (Spanish)  "Merci" (French) "danke Schion" (German) "Arigato" (Japanese) ("Ankthay ouyay" (Pig Latin) Superb! Did you say "PLEASE" or "Cheese" And they  should know what to say "EXCUSE ME" Excuse me!!! Excuse me. "Oh, Ms. Otter" "Excuse me, Mr. Bee, I need to run and check on something." I can  say EXCUSE ME in five languages. "Dispenseme" (Spanish) "Pardonnez-moi" (French) "Entschuldigen Sie" (German) "Sumimasen" (Japanese) "Excuseway emay" (Pig Latin) oops  Well "P-U" is the same in any language! It worked in rehearsal. Excuse me for interrupting  your reading but I heard you say Please not "CHEESE." Otters should be HONEST. That means  they should KEEP THEIR PROMISES. My word is as good as GOLD (fish)! NOT LIE I never lie - it makes my whiskers itch. NOT CHEAT. Cheating makes my whiskers itch,  too . . . i wonder if i should see a doctor? I'd like otters to be CONSIDERATE. You know . . . Being a GOOD LISTENER. - "I had a nightmare." Asking before BORROWING something. - "May I?" NOTLITTERING BEING PATIENT - "Please wait" CARING for all CREATURES - (big and small) OPENING THE DOOR for someone - "After you" BEING ON TIME RESPECTING THE ELDERLY - "Good afternoon, Mrs. Duck" "Hello Dearie" HELPING NEIGHBOR untangle EARS. It's always good to have a considerate  neighbor. It wouldn't hurt otters to be KIND. (Everyone appreciates a kind act no matter how  bad it smells) Oh and what's that word? . . . "COOPERATE!" Otters should learn to cooperate. Did someone say  "OPERATE?" CO-operate: to work well together. We know how to co-OTTER-ate!" I see otters like to play. I hope they know how to play fair. PLAY FAIR Otter's rules for  FAIR PLAY Be a good sport Play by the Rules Take turns Include everyone  (even BEES) (oww!) I'd like it if we could SHARE things: Our favorite books, "Harry Otter" "Goldilocks and the  Three Hares" Our favorite activities, Otter Totter Go Fish "OK!" Our favorite treats (hmmm... maybe not the  treats) I hope otters won't tease me about: My "Doo-Dee-Doo" song My extra-large swim fins. My "bad hare days"  i hope otters won't tease ANYONE about ANYTHING. "Teasing is mean." "It's the worst!" "It's worse than  having a clam snap shut on your nose!" I think otters should APOLOGIZE when they do something wrong. " I'm sorry i used your ear as a tissue." And I hope they can be FORGIVING when I do   something wrong. I'm sorry I called you "SNOTTE" Oh, you! [giggle] So there. That's how I'd like otters to treat me.  You see Mr. Rabbit, I told you it was simple! Right! Just DOO-DEE-DOO onto otters as you would  have otters DOO-DEE-DOO onto you [Applause] "Do not do to others that which would  anger you if others did it to you"   -Socrates (the Greek philosopher) circa 470-399  B.C. The End Now it's time to start the quiz! Mr Otter greets Mr. Rabbit each morning with a cheerful hello, a nice smile,   and a good eye contact. Mr. Otter is being: Friendly  Honest or Considerate The answer is Friendly Mrs Otter is being -------- when she says please, thank  you and excuse me. Cooperate Polite or Honest The answer is Polite Brother Otter always keeps  his promises, does not lie and does not cheat. He is very --------. Polite, Friendly or  Honest The answer is Honest [Music] When Sister Otter helps her neighbors and opens the door for others, she is being ----------------. Honest, Cooperate or Considerate The answer is  Considerate Baby Otter ------------- when he is a good sport, plays by the rules and includes everyone. Shares,  Plays fair, Forgives The answer is Plays Fair Brother and Sister Otter ------- their favorite books, toys and treats with each other. Cooperate Plays fair or Share The answer is Share All otters ------- when they do something wrong. Apologize, Share or Forgive The answer is Apologize [Music] All otters are -------- when others do something wrong Polite, Friendly or Forgiving The answer is  Forgiving Do unto otters sounds just like . . . The Golden Rule, The Golden Pool or The Golden Tool The answer is the Golden Rule The Golden Rule is . . . an eye for an eye I told you so, Do unto others as you would have them to onto you The answer is Do unto others as you would have them do unto you Discover your favorite bedtime story creatively read by me! description: Kind: captions Language: en Story time is fun! This is my way of encouraging  kids like me to read learn and have fun!  Come join me, for a story time with Lorenzo. Too much glue  Creatively read and adapted by Lorenzo written by Jason Lefebvre illustrated by Zach Retz  Our art teacher says, "Too much glue never dries."  She reminds us, "Glue raindrops, not puddles!" And she warns me, "Matty, too much glue!"  But my dad and i love glue! At home, we make blue glasses, glue mustaches   and even glue bouncy balls. Mom is happy to help.  So during art class, I find  the fullest bottles of glue.  i tip them over and squeeze. Ploooop! Glue squishes from the orange  tips and slops all over.  Sequins and googly eyes  float around in a gluey lake.  Then it's time for the most  important decoration . . . Geronimo!!!  i belly flop onto the table and roll around,  letting the glue and everything else cover me "Time to go onto the drying rack!" i announce. But when i try to pull   myself off the table, i boing right back down! "Too much glue, Matty! Too much glue!" my teacher   squawks. Tthis is bad. There's only half an hour  until the end of the school and all i can do is   lift my head, wave my hands, and wiggle my feet. The rest of me is a blucky stucky mess!  "Can somebody help me?" i call. While my teacher breathes into a paper  bag, Noah shouts. "Let's lasso him!"   Izzy, Noah and Owen get to work. Soon i'm roped from all sides like a rodeo pony.  But when they tried to pull me out... SNAP  The lassoes break, leaving colorful  octopus tentacles everywhere.  the glue is too strong and now i'm  a clingy stringy blocky stucky mess "Don't worry Matty. We know what to do!"  shout Luke and Grace from across the room.  "Is that a tow truck?" i ask as  they wheel the contraption over   and stick a plastic hook into my suit of glue.  My friends pull one way and the glue pulls the  other. CREAK! CLICK! CREAK! CLICK! until ... The tow truck explodes and  plastic bricks ran all over.  Now I'm a clicky bricky, clingy  stringy blucky stucky mess.  The school nurse bursts in  and checks my temperature.  "98.6, Sorry. No fever. i  can't send you home early."  She dabs and pats me like I'm spilled juice, but the more she plots the more the glue spreads.  Soon i'm a melted mummy clicky bricky  clingy stringy blucky stucky mess.  Then the principal comes in. He takes one look at me, sticks a note   on my belly and leaves. Seeing my teacher huffing  and puffing like a train gives me a great idea.  i whisper it to Hailey and Owen. The final bell rings   and everyone freezes - except Owen and Hailey. "It's the biggest one we can make!"  they shout, furiously flapping  a huge paper fan at me.  Then just as i'm thinking, I'll be  a note-on-my-tummy, melted mummy,   clicky bricky clingy stringy blucky stucky glue  boy for the rest of my life, my plan works!  Something my teacher said  could never happen, happens.  The glue dries! But I'm still stuck and now i hear footsteps.  The door starts to open. My father and some other carpool parents walk in.  Dad comes closer and inspects me. Then he peels me off the   table - glue, yarn, bricks and all. He spins me around. No one makes a sound.  Then dad smiles. "Matty, you're a masterpiece!" He holds me up for everyone to admire.  My friends all cheer. [Applause] The car ride home was interesting.  Mom is speechless when dad brings me in  the house but he knows just what to do.  "Well, kiddo." Dad says, "some beautiful things only happen once,   and this is one of those things." He gently grips the dried glue   in front of my neck and behind my  collar peels me open like a ripe banana!  Now it's Dad's turn to glue, and he seals  up the sides of the me shaped work of art.  "i bet it would take all the glue in the art room  to make a YOU-shaped work of art, Dad!" I say.  Dad laughs. Then he glues a big magnet to the  back of my project and hangs it on the fridge.  During dinner we sneak peeks at my masterpiece. And after dinner...  ...we take the principal's note very seriously From the desk of Elmer G Stuckey  Please encourage Matty to  use tape instead of glue. The End Now it's time to start the quiz! What is the setting of the story?  kitchen school  backyard or the principal's office  the answer is the school  next question What do matty and his family like to do?  play outside go to school  watch tv or make things with glue  the answer is make things with glue  What happens to Matty at school? he makes a picture with glue  he gets sent to the principal's office he has a normal day with no weird things  he uses too much glue and gets stuck the answer is  he uses too much glue and gets stuck Who finally rescues Matty?  the president his best friend  his dad or his mom  the answer is his dad  Kaboom, creak and snap are all examples of simile  onomatopoeia personification  or metaphor the answer is onomatopoeia  What does Dad do with the artwork at the end  of the story? crumples it up and throws it away  mails it to Matty's grandparents or puts a magnet and hangs it on the fridge  the answer is puts on a magnet and hangs it on the fridge  What is the artwork at the end? a chalk drawing  a yarn picture a glue suit  or the mona lisa the answer is a glue suit and that's the end If you like this video, like and subscribe [Music]

Ernestine is in over her head. Monday through Sunday, Ernestine’s week is packed with after-school lessons—tuba, knitting, sculpting, water ballet, yoga, yodeling, and karate. Overwhelmed and exhausted, Ernestine decides to take matters into her own hands and heads off to the park with her Nanny where she builds a fort, watches the clouds, and plays all kinds of unstructured and imaginative games. But when a teacher calls Ernestine's mom to report that she has not shown up for yodeling, her parents search everywhere until at last they hear their daughter's laughter coming from the park. Ernestine tells her parents what a wonderful afternoon she's had, and explains her plight, asking, "I like my lessons, but can't I stop some of them?" This saga hilariously captures the dilemma of the modern-day over-scheduled child in riotous color and absurd extremes. A delightful heroine, Ernestine will be sure to put “play” back on everyone’s agenda, demonstrating that in today’s overscheduled world, everyone needs the joy of play and the simple wonders of childhood.

When the forecast calls for snow, one little boy is thrilled. He keeps peeking outside to see if it’s snowing - but he only looks up! His single-minded focus on the sky makes him completely miss the increasingly comical chaos occurring outside his door, which includes a monster truck, a firetruck, escaped monkeys, and carousing clowns. The boy bides his time and tries to wait patiently, but waiting is boring! As the hours go by and not a snowflake is seen, the boy begins to worry that it might NEVER snow again! That’s no fun! If only he would notice all of the wacky events unfolding outside! Finally, when the boy is just about to give up, the long-awaited white stuff arrives with a single jubilant word - SNOW! All of his frustration instantly disappears, and the boy rushes outside declaring, “I knew it would snow! I knew it!” Still oblivious to the pandemonium around him, he concludes, “Nothing’s as fun as snow!”

This is cute book featuring lots of different animals and colors.

video_title: 🔠📚Book League Character Alphabet Aerobics - ABC Rap Read Aloud
description:
This is a music video of my hype girl Scarlett and I performing a song I wrote and produced. In the song I go through the alphabet from A-Z using only picture book character names. As you know, I love children's books (any kind of book really) and believe that reading is the most important thing you can do for the brain, especially young brains.  Unfortunately, as a society, we are doing less and less of it, so this is an attempt to promote reading to children in a different way than what is being done. Also, it was super fun to make! Please let me know in the comments which characters you wish were added. There are many that I really wanted to add, but some letters had so many (especially P) that I had to leave out really good ones. And some letters (I'm looking at you X!) I had to scrounge to come up with any. Most of the characters are from picture books, but there are a few middle grade book characters thrown in there too. My hope is that the kids, parents, teachers, caregivers, and anyone who likes reading or music will have as much fun watching this as I did making it.

This song was inspired by the rap group Blackalicious. They came out with a song called Alphabet Aerobics on their EP A2G in 1999. It's one of my favorite all time hip-hop songs and Gift of Gab is a legend. I could never hope to even come close to replicating what he does, but it sure was fun. 
 
The beat came from Ryan R. Sullivan (AKA Sullybop). He is primarily a podcast coach and trainer, but is also a rapper and super cool guy. If you have a podcast, check him out! https://www.youtube.com/c/sullybop

I learned how to mix and master the song from YouTube of course. Primarily from this channel: https://www.youtube.com/@KelliMusic. Kelli is a fantastic rapper and does how to videos for mixing and mastering on Adobe Audition. He also has a ton of different effect presets available for purchase. His videos are awesome. 

My editor Abhishek is amazing. He put together everything I had in my head and more. Totally exceeded my expectations and made it happen even better than I thought it be.  Thanks Bud!!

The hype girl is my daughter, Scarlett. She's definitely my favorite character in the video.....BY FAR!!!
